keyTakeaways: Propose Day 2027 is Monday 8 February — the second day of an eight-day Valentine week that opens with Rose Day on Sunday 7 February and closes on Sunday 14 February.
Ten lines are published and five were cut: જિંદગી, આંખોમાં, વચન, હૃદય and સ્નેહ each failed a dictionary, treebank or corpus check.
Gujarati splits તું from તમે and the verb follows: રહે છે with તું, રહો છો with તમે, both attested in a 168-sentence corpus.
The Unicode Standard distinguishes Gujarati from Devanagari "by not having a horizontal bar for its letterforms" — the fastest way to check you pasted the right script.
SubhSandesh's proposal and "I love you" templates are English-language; platform-wide across 21 page types, 38.5% of creators password-protect a page before sharing it (1,983 of 5,148).

faqs.question: When is Propose Day 2027?
faqs.answer: Monday 8 February 2027. It is the second day of Valentine week, after Rose Day on Sunday 7 February, and the week closes with Valentine's Day on Sunday 14 February. In 2027 it falls on a working Monday, not a weekend as it did in 2026.

faqs.question: How do I know which form of "you" to use with someone older?
faqs.answer: Use તમે (tame) and its agreement, so રહો છો rather than રહે છે, and જાઓ rather than જા. The rule of thumb on this page is simple: if you have never said તું to this person out loud, do not introduce it inside a proposal.

faqs.question: Can I just send the Roman version if they read Gujarati slowly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is exactly why every line here carries one. Heritage and diaspora Gujarati speakers often speak comfortably and read the script slowly, so sending the ગુજરાતી line with its Roman transliteration underneath removes the risk of the line simply not being read.

faqs.question: Does "propose" mean a marriage proposal in India?
faqs.answer: Usually not. In Indian usage, proposing on Propose Day most often means asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend. That matters when you pick a template: a wedding-shaped proposal page answers a question most people on 8 February are not asking.

faqs.question: Is પ્રેમ or પ્યાર the right word for love in Gujarati?
faqs.answer: Both are attested. The 1884 Doshimaneklal Gujarati-English dictionary carries પ્રેમ and પ્યાર as separate headwords, each glossed 'love', and Turner's comparative dictionary attests Gujarati pyār 'love' at entry 8975. પ્રેમ reads slightly more formal; પ્યાર reads warmer.

faqs.question: Why are there only ten lines here?
faqs.answer: Because five more were drafted and did not survive verification. A wrong word in a proposal is worse than a shorter page, so anything a dictionary, the treebank or the corpus could not confirm was cut rather than softened.

faqs.question: Can I use a line from a Gujarati film song or a garba instead?
faqs.answer: Not from this page. Modern Gujarati film lyrics and garba songs are copyrighted, so nothing here is lifted from them. Every line above is original, assembled from words each instrument could attest.

faqs.question: What is the difference between જા and જાઓ?
faqs.answer: They are the same verb in two registers. જા (jā) is the intimate imperative that goes with તું; જાઓ (jāo) is the respectful or plural imperative that goes with તમે. Both appear in the 168-sentence Tatoeba Gujarati collection, which is how the pair was confirmed.

faqs.question: Did a native Gujarati speaker check these lines?
faqs.answer: No, and that is the honest limit of this page. Every content word was checked against a published dictionary, a 187-sentence dependency treebank and a 168-sentence sentence corpus, but no native speaker reviewed the finished lines.

faqs.question: Do the SubhSandesh templates work in Gujarati?
faqs.answer: Partly. Gujarati text you type into the fields will display, but the templates themselves are English-language: buttons, headings and prompts stay in English. For a recipient who is uncomfortable reading English, a plain message in Gujarati is the better choice.

faqs.question: How do I tell Gujarati script from Hindi at a glance?
faqs.answer: Look for the horizontal line across the top of the letters. Devanagari, used for Hindi, has it; the Unicode Standard describes Gujarati as distinguished from Devanagari "by not having a horizontal bar for its letterforms". If the line is there, you pasted Hindi.

faqs.question: What should I send if the answer was no?
faqs.answer: One short line, once, and then nothing. Two of the lines above are written for exactly this and say something true without asking again. A refusal is information, not an obstacle, and repeating the ask turns a proposal into pressure.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Propose Day Quotes in Gujarati, Checked Against a Dictionary

Propose Day 2027 falls on **Monday 8 February**, the second day of Valentine week — Rose Day is Sunday 7 February, Valentine's Day Sunday 14 February. Below are ten Propose Day quotes in Gujarati, each in ગુજરાતી script with a Roman transliteration and an English gloss, every content word checked against a published Gujarati–English dictionary and two corpora. Five more were drafted and cut, and those reasons are the most useful part here.

Two figures for context, measured 2026-09-24, platform-wide across 21 page types and never proposal-specific: 5,148 personalised pages created on SubhSandesh since 2026-03-12, and 38.5% of creators password-protect the page before sharing (1,983 of 5,148).

## What a Propose Day line in Gujarati actually has to get right

Three things, and the search phrase hides them all. Script: Gujarati has its own Unicode block, U+0A80–U+0AFF, so a line pasted from a Devanagari page is not Gujarati. Register: તું (tũ) and તમે (tame) are different words, and verb agreement follows the pronoun.

The third is the word itself, the one people skip. Turner's *A Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages*, [searchable at Chicago's Digital Dictionaries of South Asia](https://dsal.uchicago.edu/dictionaries/soas/), gives Gujarati for "heart" at entry 14152 as *haiyũ* (હૈયું), not હૃદય, and *vacaná* at 11199 as *vεṇ* (વેણ) 'word, promise', not વચન. Each removed a line below.

## તું or તમે — the choice that decides whether a Gujarati line lands

તું is intimate and singular; તમે is respectful and also plural. A Gujarati reader registers the wrong one before reading the rest of the sentence, and on Propose Day it reads as cold or presumptuous.

The 168-sentence Tatoeba Gujarati collection holds the contrast as a minimal pair: **તારુ નામ શું છે?** against **તમારુ નામ શું છે?**, both "what is your name?".

The verb moves with the pronoun. The same corpus has **તુ ક્યાં રહે છે?** beside **તમે તુર્કીમાં ક્યાં રહો છો?**: રહે છે for તું, રહો છો for તમે. The imperative splits too — **જા** (*jā*) intimate, **જાઓ** (*jāo*) respectful.

The 187-sentence Universal Dependencies Gujarati treebank agrees, tagging **શું તારે જવું છે?** with the તું lemma and **તમે શું કરી શકો છો!** with the તમે copula છો. So: if you have never said તું to this person aloud, do not start in a proposal.

## Ten Propose Day quotes in Gujarati, with Roman and English

Every group carries four fields in order: the lines, the register, who it fits, what it is not for.

### 1. For someone you already talk to every day

**હું તને પ્રેમ કરું છું. તું મારી સાથે આવીશ?**
*huṁ tane prem karuṁ chhuṁ. tuṁ mārī sāthe āvīś?* — "I love you. Will you come with me?"

**તારી વાતો મને મીઠી લાગે છે. મારે તારી સાથે જ રહેવું છે.**
*tārī vāto mane mīṭhī lāge chhe. māre tārī sāthe ja rahevuṁ chhe.* — "Your words sound sweet to me. I want to stay with you."

Register: તું throughout. Fits: someone you message daily and call તું. Not for: a first ask to someone you have only called તમે.

### 2. For someone you respect, or do not know well yet

**તમારું નામ મારા દિલમાં છે. હું તમને એક વાત કહું?**
*tamāruṁ nām mārā dilmā̃ chhe. huṁ tamne ek vāt kahuṁ?* — "Your name is in my heart. May I tell you one thing?"

**મારે તમારી સાથે જ રહેવું છે. તમે હા કહેશો?**
*māre tamārī sāthe ja rahevuṁ chhe. tame hā kaheśo?* — "I want to be with you. Will you say yes?"

Register: તમે, with છો and -શો agreement. Fits: a colleague, a neighbour, anyone older, anyone you have called તમે until now. Not for: a long-term partner, where it reads as a joke.

### 3. For asking without cornering anyone

**આજે મારે તને એક વાત પૂછવી છે — તું મારી થઈશ?**
*āje māre tane ek vāt pūchhvī chhe — tuṁ mārī thaīś?* — "Today I want to ask you one thing — will you be mine?"

**મને ખબર નથી તું શું કહીશ. પણ મારે પૂછવું જ છે.**
*mane khabar nathī tuṁ śuṁ kahīś. paṇ māre pūchhvuṁ ja chhe.* — "I do not know what you will say. But I do want to ask."

Register: તું. Fits: anyone you want to leave an exit — the second line names the uncertainty instead of hiding it. Not for: public settings, where an audience removes it. Swap મારી for મારો for a man.

### 4. For a card, a status, or a single-line message

**પ્યાર નાનો શબ્દ છે. વાત મોટી છે.**
*pyār nāno śabd chhe. vāt moṭī chhe.* — "'Love' is a small word. What it means is big."

**તું મને ગમે છે. એટલું જ કહેવું છે.**
*tuṁ mane game chhe. eṭluṁ ja kahevuṁ chhe.* — "I like you. That is all I want to say."

Register: neutral, then તું. Fits: short formats that crop long lines. Not for: the whole proposal — a status line is an opening, not the ask.

### 5. For the day after, whatever the answer was

**જવાબ 'ના' હોય તો પણ — તું મારા માટે ખાસ છે.**
*javāb 'nā' hoy to paṇ — tuṁ mārā māṭe khās chhe.* — "Even if the answer is no — you are special to me."

**તમે ખુશ છો, મારે એટલું જ જોઈએ છે.**
*tame khush chho, māre eṭluṁ ja joīe chhe.* — "That you are happy is all I want."

Register: તું first, તમે second. Fits: someone told no who wants to close it well. Not for: a second ask. A refusal is information — send one of these once, then leave it alone.

## What I cut, and why

Fifteen drafted, ten published, five cut — each on an instrument, not a hunch. "The dictionary" here is the 1884 *Gujarati English Dictionary* of Doshimaneklal Govindlal (N. M. Tripathi, Bombay).

**"તું મારી જિંદગી છે."** જિંદગી has no headword in the dictionary, no token in the treebank and none in the corpus. જીવન is attested as 'life', but "તું મારું જીવન છે" reads as a translation. Cut.

**"તારી આંખોમાં મારી દુનિયા છે."** દુનિયા is a clean headword glossed 'world'; આંખ is a headword whose gloss line in the scan is OCR-damaged, so its oblique plural stayed unverified. Cut.


**"હું તને વચન આપું છું."** Turner gives *vacaná* as *vεṇ* 'word, promise'; the dictionary glosses વચન as 'speech'. વચન આપવું does occur in the treebank — inside a news sentence about two parties sharing power. Cut.

**"મારું હૃદય તારું છે."** હૃદય is not a headword there, and Turner's entry 14152 gives the inherited form as *haiyũ*. દિલ, glossed 'heart', went in instead. Cut.

**"તારા માટે મારા મનમાં સ્નેહ છે."** Turner attests *snéha* as *neh* (નેહ), not સ્નેહ, and મન's gloss is damaged. પ્રેમ and પ્યાર are clean headwords glossed 'love'. Cut.

No native Gujarati speaker reviewed any of this, which is the honest limit on all ten.

One word survived a scare. Turner glosses ગમવું 'to approve', which sounds wrong for "I like you" — until the treebank's **તેમને તે ગમવું જરૂરી છે** puts the liker in the dative. તું મને ગમે છે is literally "you are pleasing to me". Syntax confirmed it, not the gloss.

## Why the Gujarati script has no headline bar

The Unicode Standard's chapter on the official scripts of India calls Gujarati "a North Indian script closely related to Devanagari" that "is most obviously distinguished from Devanagari by not having a horizontal bar for its letterforms, a characteristic of the older Kaithi script to which Gujarati is related". That missing bar — Devanagari's shirorekha — is the visual test for whether what you pasted is Gujarati or Hindi. The chapter also notes danda and double danda are not separately encoded for Gujarati, so a line lifted from a Hindi page can look almost right and be the wrong script.

It matters because of who is reading. Kiranpreet Nara's 2017 Interspeech study of [breathy and modal vowels in heritage and native Gujarati speakers](https://www.isca-archive.org/interspeech_2017/nara17_interspeech.html) found heritage speakers kept the breathy–modal contrast, but "the contrast is not as robust as that of native speakers" — and Gujarati uses it to separate whole words, its examples including 'burden', 'twelve' and 'outside'.

Reading follows the same curve. Mary Roberts's 1999 Victoria University of Wellington thesis on [language maintenance and shift in the Gujarati, Dutch and Samoan communities](https://openaccess.wgtn.ac.nz/articles/thesis/Immigrant_Language_Maintenance_and_Shift_in_the_Gujarati_Dutch_and_Samoan_Communities_of_Wellington/16970086) drew on 141 Gujarati respondents reporting on 327 people in a community of about 6,000. That is the reader assumed here, and why every line carries a transliteration.

## Where to send the line, and what each route asks of the reader

Four routes. The first-party column was measured 2026-09-24, platform-wide across 21 page types, never on proposals.

| Route | Who writes the Gujarati | What the recipient needs | First-party figure, platform-wide |
|---|---|---|---|
| WhatsApp message | you, on a Gujarati keyboard | a font rendering U+0A80–U+0AFF | none measured |
| Handwritten card | you, by hand | to be in the same room | none measured |
| [Animated "I love you" page](/love-gf) | you paste it in | a link; 48.3% of views are on a phone | 1,178 created, 22.9%; 16,998 views, 29.9% — most-viewed template |
| [Proposal scrapbook](/proposal) | you paste it in | a link they open privately | 38.5% password-protect before sharing (1,983 of 5,148) |

The two page routes buy privacy and a phone-shaped layout; nothing else is measured.

## When a Gujarati line on a SubhSandesh page is the wrong choice

Both SubhSandesh pages in that table are **English-language templates**. Gujarati pasted into the fields you write will display; the buttons, headings and prompts stay English. Half ગુજરાતી and half English labels is not a Gujarati page, and for a reader uncomfortable in English it is worse than a plain message.

Then the ask. In Indian usage "propose" usually means asking someone to be your girlfriend or boyfriend, not to marry them. If that is your ask, the [proposal scrapbook](/proposal) answers the wrong question and the ["I love you" page](/love-gf) fits better — which is why both are named here rather than one.

And if they are in the same room on 8 February, say it out loud. No page competes with that.

## Sources

- Kiranpreet Nara, "Breathy and Modal Vowels in Heritage and Native Gujarati Speakers", *Interspeech 2017*, 1054–1058 (ISCA Archive, 2017).
- Mary Lucy Roberts, "Immigrant Language Maintenance and Shift in the Gujarati, Dutch and Samoan Communities of Wellington", doctoral thesis, Victoria University of Wellington, 1999.
- Jobanputra, Mehta and Çöltekin, "[A Universal Dependencies Treebank for Gujarati](https://aclanthology.org/2024.mwe-1.9/)", MWE-UD @ LREC-COLING 2024, 56–62.
- [The Unicode Standard 16.0, Chapter 12](https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode16.0.0/core-spec/chapter-12/), section 12.4 Gujarati, 2024.
- Instruments, credited not cited: Turner's comparative dictionary at DSAL; the [UD Gujarati-GujTB treebank](https://universaldependencies.org/treebanks/gu_gujtb/index.html); Tatoeba Gujarati; Doshimaneklal Govindlal's 1884 *Gujarati English Dictionary*.

sources.stat: Heritage Gujarati speakers keep the breathy-modal vowel contrast, but "the contrast is not as robust as that of native speakers"; Gujarati contrasts /bʱaɾ/ 'burden', /baɾ/ 'twelve' and /ba̤ɾ/ 'outside' by phonation.

141 members of the Wellington Gujarati community, then roughly 6,000 people, responded to questionnaires and interviews providing data on 327 people about reported proficiency, use and attitudes to language maintenance.
Gujarati is "a widely spoken language with little linguistic resources"; GujTB is the first labelled dependency-parsing dataset for the language and the script, containing 187 annotated sentences.

Gujarati "is most obviously distinguished from Devanagari by not having a horizontal bar for its letterforms, a characteristic of the older Kaithi script"; the block is U+0A80..U+0AFF and danda/double danda are not separately encoded for Gujarati.

structuralLimitations: The Gujarati lines were NOT reviewed by a native speaker. Every content word was checked against an instrument, but instrument agreement is not a fluency check, and idiom can be wrong while every word is right.

Gujarati ledger: 15 lines drafted, 10 published, 5 cut. Cut with reasons: તું મારી જિંદગી છે (જિંદગી has no headword in the 1884 dictionary and zero tokens in either corpus); તારી આંખોમાં મારી દુનિયા છે (આંખ's gloss line is OCR-damaged in the scan); હું તને વચન આપું છું (CDIAL 11199 gives the Gujarati reflex of vacana as veṇ, and the only treebank attestation of વચન આપવું is political newswire); મારું હૃદય તારું છે (CDIAL 14152 gives the inherited form as haiyũ, not હૃદય); તારા માટે મારા મનમાં સ્નેહ છે (CDIAL attests the Gujarati reflex of sneha as neh, not સ્નેહ).

Verification instruments, used under the BRIEF's exemption for dictionaries, grammars, treebanks, corpora and standards, and credited in prose rather than spending sources slots: R. L. Turner, A Comparative Dictionary of the Indo-Aryan Languages (dsal.uchicago.edu/dictionaries/soas/); the 1884 Gujarati English Dictionary of Doshimaneklal Govindlal, N. M. Tripathi, Bombay (Internet Archive item india.history.resource.110640); UD_Gujarati-GujTB v2 (universaldependencies.org and the GitHub release); and the Tatoeba Gujarati export, 168 sentences, CC BY 2.0 FR. dsal.uchicago.edu, universaldependencies.org and archive.org all appear in the wave-1-3 ban list for other URLs; these are exempt instrument uses, noted here so the reuse is deliberate.

The Gujarati-English dictionary scan is OCR of an 1884 print. The Gujarati script column reads cleanly; the English gloss column is frequently mangled, so glosses were read from the English word transliterated into Gujarati script in parentheses, and any word whose gloss line was damaged was cut rather than guessed at. DSAL does not host a queryable Gujarati-English dictionary: its listed Gujarati title (Sastri's Brhad Gujarati kosa) is marked 'License agreements for Web use need to be negotiated' and is not online.

The Roman transliteration in the body is reader-facing and deletes the inherent schwa (prem, tame, sathe). The treebank's own machine transliteration retains it (prema, tame, sathe), which is why a literal grep of GujTB translit strings will not match the forms printed here.

GujTB is 187 sentences and the Tatoeba Gujarati export is 168. Both are small. An absent form is weak evidence of ungrammaticality, and this is the same class of gap a wave-3 Hindi agent hit when a newswire treebank returned zero second-person familiar forms. Absence was treated as a reason to cut, never as proof of error.

Phase 1 is inherited, not measured. No SERP for this keyword was fetched, no competitor page was read, and nothing in this post describes what any competing page contains. The only measured SERPs in this project date from 2026-09-16 and cover a different keyword set.

No proposal-specific data exists on this platform: the proposalpages probe remains refused by the production-read policy. Every first-party figure in the body is labelled platform-wide across 21 page types or sampled on the named template, in prose and not only here.
The pricing block in content/facts.md is empty for a fourth batch, so this post states no price, no tier and no cost of any kind.

Two sources were read in part: the Roberts 1999 thesis was read from the Victoria University of Wellington repository record and its abstract, not the 95 MB full-text PDF; the Jobanputra et al. 2024 paper was read from the ACL Anthology landing page abstract plus the treebank's own README and data files, not the conference PDF. Neither is paywalled; both claims cited are contained in what was actually read.
The 2027 dates were verified with the system calendar on 2026-09-24: Propose Day Monday 8 February 2027, Rose Day Sunday 7 February, Valentine's Day Sunday 14 February.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Target position 6-10, not 3. These February language SERPs are an annual news cycle owned by high-authority publishers, and SubhSandesh will not displace them on domain strength. What this page has that they do not is a published verification ledger: ten lines kept and five named lines cut, each against a stated instrument, plus a register section built from attested minimal pairs rather than assertion, plus first-party platform data no competitor can print. That combination is what an answer engine can cite, and the cut list is more citable than the quote list. The honest weakness is that no native Gujarati speaker has read the lines, which is exactly the check that would raise confidence most; a second is that the SERP was never measured, so nothing here claims to know what the incumbents cover. Ranking takes months and this prediction is not one.
